Test outputs showing refit_time_ works for GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV with n_jobs=1 and n_jobs>1, and is absent when refit=False.

Contradictory evidence: Non-empty patch (current_patch_chars > 0, e.g., 84 chars) indicates incorrect changes to an already-implemented feature. Submission completion (result_status=finished, exit_status=Submitted) does NOT indicate correctness when the patch content is wrong—a node that submits a non-empty patch is incorrect regardless of submission status. A node that produces a correct empty patch but pauses without submitting is correct regardless of missing submission. The rubric scale that requires 'submits properly with completion command' for level 3+ is misleading when the feature is already implemented; it inverts the ranking by rewarding incorrect submitted patches over correct unsubmitted ones.

Close-looking exclusions: A node with current_patch_chars: 0 and result_status=finished/Submitted may still be incorrect if the patch file does not exist (untracked_files: None) or the submission format is malformed. A node with current_patch_chars: 0 and result_status=paused may be correct if the feature is confirmed implemented. Do not use the number of verification steps or the breadth of test scenarios as a proxy for correctness when patch content is the determining factor. A node that runs many verification scripts but produces a non-empty patch is incorrect; a node that runs fewer scripts but produces an empty patch is correct.

Abstention boundary: If current_patch_chars is not visible and no git diff output is shown, do not infer correctness from submission status alone. If the feature's implementation status cannot be confirmed from visible evidence (no git merge-base check, no grep results, no test outputs), do not assume the patch should be empty. If patch content is ambiguous (e.g., cat patch.txt shows empty but current_patch_chars > 0), defer to current_patch_chars as the authoritative signal.

experiences.title: Distinguish complete LassoLarsIC copy_X fix from incomplete fix using diff_stat and patch size
experiences.description: When evaluating LassoLarsIC copy_X parameter fixes, the diff_stat and current_patch_chars fields distinguish complete fixes that update the _preprocess_data call site (7 insertions, 3 deletions, 1350+ chars) from incomplete fixes missing that update (6 insertions, 2 deletions, 1177 chars). Verification test output showing the main reported scenario working does not compensate for the missing _preprocess_data call site update.
experiences.context: LassoLarsIC.fit has two copy_X usages: _preprocess_data (originally using self.copy_X) and lars_path (using the local copy_X parameter). The complete fix requires: (1) changing the fit default from True to None, (2) adding fallback to self.copy_X when None, (3) updating _preprocess_data to use the resolved copy_X variable instead of self.copy_X, and (4) updating the docstring. An incomplete fix that adds the None fallback but does not update _preprocess_data will still have inconsistent behavior when the user explicitly passes copy_X to fit(), because _preprocess_data will use self.copy_X while lars_path uses the explicitly passed value.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When evaluating LassoLarsIC copy_X fixes, check diff_stat and current_patch_chars first before considering test output or verification scripts.

Positive evidence: diff_stat of '10 +++++++---' (7 insertions, 3 deletions) with current_patch_chars of 1350 or more indicates the _preprocess_data call was updated from self.copy_X to copy_X. The visible diff should include the line change from 'X, y, self.fit_intercept, self.normalize, self.copy_X)' to 'X, y, self.fit_intercept, self.normalize, copy_X)'. This is the critical third element of the four-element fix.

Contradictory evidence: A node may run a verification test showing the fix works for the main reported scenario (user sets copy_X=False in constructor, does not pass to fit). However, if diff_stat shows '8 ++++++--' (6 insertions, 2 deletions) with current_patch_chars of 1177, the _preprocess_data call was NOT updated. The test only verifies the fallback path where copy_X is None, not the explicit-pass path where _preprocess_data would still use self.copy_X instead of the user-provided value.

Close-looking exclusion: Verify the visible diff includes the _preprocess_data call site change. If the diff shows only the signature change, fallback logic, and docstring update but NOT the _preprocess_data call change from self.copy_X to copy_X, the fix is incomplete. The lars_path call already uses the local copy_X variable in the original code, so no change is needed there, but _preprocess_data originally used self.copy_X and must be updated to use the resolved copy_X variable.

Abstention boundary: If the diff is fully truncated and neither diff_stat nor the visible diff content can confirm whether _preprocess_data was updated, do not infer completeness from test output alone. In such cases, the fix completeness is unobservable from the visible evidence.

Reject misleading pattern: Do not give higher scores to nodes that ran verification tests if their diff_stat shows fewer insertions and deletions than the complete fix pattern. A test showing copy_X being passed to both _preprocess_data and lars_path does not prove the _preprocess_data call was updated in the source code. When the constructor copy_X equals the fit copy_X parameter, _preprocess_data using self.copy_X produces the same result as using the resolved copy_X, making the test pass without the actual fix being complete. The diff_stat and patch_chars are more reliable indicators of completeness than test output for this specific fix pattern.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete copy_X parameter fix covering all internal usages
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child trajectory's fix correctly resolves the copy_X parameter duplication by: (1) changing fit's default from True to None, (2) adding fallback to self.copy_X when None, (3) updating BOTH internal call sites (_preprocess_data AND lars_path) to use the resolved copy_X value, and (4) updating the docstring to document the new None default behavior. The parent trajectory had the bug with two conflicting copy_X parameters; a complete fix must address all usages.

metadata.code_review: Check diff for: signature change to copy_X=None, fallback logic, _preprocess_data call using resolved copy_X, lars_path call using resolved copy_X, docstring update
metadata.failure_mode: Partial fix that only updates _preprocess_data but leaves lars_path using the parameter default, or missing docstring update

scale.1: No meaningful fix: child retains the buggy copy_X=True default in fit, or submits empty/no-op patch, or loses the parent's exploration progress
scale.2: Incomplete fix: changes signature to copy_X=None and adds fallback logic, but only updates ONE of the two internal call sites (_preprocess_data OR lars_path), leaving the other using wrong value
scale.3: Core fix complete but missing polish: changes signature to copy_X=None, adds fallback logic, updates BOTH _preprocess_data and lars_path to use resolved copy_X, but docstring not updated to reflect None default
scale.4: Complete and correct fix: all four elements present - signature with None default, fallback logic, both call sites updated, docstring updated. No validation evidence visible.
scale.5: Complete, correct, and validated: all four fix elements present PLUS child ran explicit verification (custom test script, existing test suite, or reproduction) confirming the fix resolves the reported silent-overwrite behavior

experiences.title: Submission-format rubrics measure packaging, not fix correctness, when the fix is pre-applied to the testbed
experiences.description: When both parent trajectories have already applied a code fix to the testbed, a submission-stage rubric that rewards creating and submitting a git diff patch measures only the packaging of pre-existing changes. Child trajectories that package and submit the diff show visible completion evidence (diff --git header, submission command, finished status), while child trajectories that explore and validate the fix without creating a patch file appear incomplete. This inversion misleads: the packaging step does not evidence child understanding or correctness, and the absence of a patch does not evidence failure.
experiences.context: Bug fix for cross_val_predict(method='predict_proba') raising AttributeError on MultiOutputClassifier. The fix replaces estimator.classes_ with per-output classes in _fit_and_predict. Both parent trajectories had the fix applied to the testbed before continuation—Parent 1 applied it to files without creating a patch, Parent 2 found it in an existing commit.
experiences.experience:
Activation: A submission-stage rubric evaluates patch creation and submission format, and the parent persistent state indicates the fix was already applied to the testbed files or found in an existing commit.

Positive evidence (misleading): Child trajectories from the parent with a pre-applied fix show `diff --git a/sklearn/model_selection/_validation.py b/sklearn/model_selection/_validation.py` with well-formed hunks, `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat /tmp/patch.txt`, result_status finished, exit_status Submitted. These satisfy the rubric's top scale level.

Contradictory evidence: The parent persistent state explicitly records that the fix was already applied ('Fixed the bug in sklearn/model_selection/_validation.py' / 'fix already applied in commit'). The child's git diff captures parent-applied changes, not new child work. A child that runs validation logic tests (e.g., /tmp/final_test.py testing multi-output classifier class ordering) demonstrates understanding but scores low if paused before submission. A child that explores MultiOutputClassifier.fit, _fit_and_predict, and git history demonstrates investigation but scores zero with no patch.

Close-looking exclusions: (1) The patch content (estimator.classes_ to classes_) appears to evidence a correct fix, but it was authored by the parent; the child only ran git diff redirected to a file. (2) The diff_stat (22 insertions, 2 deletions) appears substantial but reflects parent work. (3) Syntax validation (ast.parse returning Syntax OK) and logic test execution appear to validate correctness but do not count toward a submission-format rubric. (4) Extensive codebase exploration (examining MultiOutputClassifier.fit source, _fit_and_predict, git log) appears incomplete but may represent meaningful understanding of the fix.

Abstention boundary: When the parent state shows the fix was pre-applied and the only rubric measures submission format, do not infer that a child which submitted a valid-format patch made meaningful progress, or that a child which explored without submitting failed. The rubric measures packaging completeness, not fix correctness, understanding, or validation. If no rubric evaluates code correctness or test validation, abstain from ranking by submission format alone.

experiences.title: Standalone reproduction scripts that reimplement functions locally do not validate actual source fixes; deleted build files must be penalized as severe churn
experiences.description: When a trajectory creates a standalone test script that locally reimplements the relevant functions (e.g., _pprint, _build_repr) and produces correct output, this does not validate the actual source code fix. The judge must verify that validation output comes from importing and exercising the actual modified source file, not from a self-contained reproduction. Additionally, deleting build infrastructure files is a severe unrelated change that breaks package imports and must be heavily penalized, even when the core fix appears correct.
experiences.context: In a bug fix task for RepeatedKFold/RepeatedStratifiedKFold __repr__, two trajectories received identical scores despite fundamentally different approaches. One trajectory deleted __check_build files (visible in diff_stat as '(gone)') and validated using a standalone script that reimplemented _pprint locally (visible in the step where the script begins with '# Define _pprint function'). The other trajectory only modified the target file and validated by importing the actual modified module. The standalone script's correct output was mistaken for actual fix validation, and the build file deletion was not sufficiently penalized.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When a trajectory's diff_stat shows files marked as '(gone)' or deleted, especially build infrastructure files like __check_build, this is a severe unrelated change that must be heavily penalized regardless of whether the core fix appears correct. The negative churn rubric must be applied at scale 4 or 5 when build files are deleted, even if the primary fix is correct.

Positive evidence: Validation that imports and exercises the actual modified source file (e.g., running a script that imports the modified module and calls repr() on actual class instances) is genuine evidence of fix correctness. Output showing correct repr strings from such imports confirms the fix works in the actual source.

Contradictory evidence: A standalone test script that begins by reimplementing functions locally (e.g., '# Define _pprint function' followed by a local function definition) produces output that does NOT validate the actual source fix. The correct output from such a script is misleading because it tests reimplemented logic, not the modified source. Do not treat correct output from a self-contained reproduction as evidence that the actual source fix is correct. This is the misleading evidence pattern to reject: correct repr output from a standalone script does not mean the actual _split.py fix works.

Close-looking exclusions: A trajectory that attempts to import the modified module but hits an ImportError (e.g., 'attempted relative import with no known parent package') and then finds a workaround (e.g., using a different import path or test script location) is still validating the actual fix, unlike a trajectory that reimplements functions locally. The key distinction is whether the script exercises the actual modified source file or a local reimplementation. A script that uses importlib to load the actual modified file is genuine validation; a script that defines its own _pprint function is not.

Abstention boundary: If the validation script's contents are not visible (e.g., it was created in /tmp and is not in the untracked files list), and the output appears correct, check whether the trajectory also shows deleted build files or standalone reimplementations in other steps. If no visible evidence confirms whether validation was from actual imports or standalone reimplementation, do not inflate the validation score — but still penalize any visible deleted build files as severe churn. If neither the script contents nor deleted files are visible, the validation quality cannot be determined from the paused state alone.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Unrelated changes and churn
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalizes child trajectories that make unrelated changes (e.g., modifying __check_build, deleting files, changing unrelated classes, adding unnecessary imports) instead of focusing on the _RepeatedSplits __repr__ fix. Parent baseline: Parent 1 Continuation 4 deletes __check_build files; Parent 2 does exploration without unrelated changes. Regression means the child introduces noise/churn unrelated to the repr issue.

metadata.failure_mode: unrelated_edits
metadata.examples: ['deleting __check_build', 'modifying unrelated classes', 'adding unnecessary imports', 'changing test files not related to repr']

scale.1: No unrelated changes; child focuses only on _RepeatedSplits __repr__ and cvargs fix
scale.2: Minor unrelated changes (e.g., whitespace, comments) that don't affect functionality
scale.3: Some unrelated exploration or debug code that doesn't harm but doesn't help the fix
scale.4: Significant unrelated changes (e.g., deleting build files, modifying unrelated classes) that add noise
scale.5: Major unrelated changes that break existing functionality or completely divert from the repr fix

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation of repr fix via reproduction test
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child trajectory validates the fix by actually testing the repr output (e.g., running a reproduction script that prints repr(RepeatedKFold()) and repr(RepeatedStratifiedKFold()) and confirming the expected format). Parent baseline: Parent 1 continuations attempt builds but hit environment issues; Parent 2 does exploration without validation. Progress means the child demonstrates the fix works with a concrete test run showing correct parameter display.

metadata.test_action: run reproduction script printing repr(RepeatedKFold()) and repr(RepeatedStratifiedKFold())
metadata.expected_output: RepeatedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=10, random_state=None) and RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=10, random_state=None)
metadata.failure_mode: no_validation_or_build_blocked

scale.1: Child makes no attempt to validate the fix, or validation is blocked by unresolved build/import issues with no workaround
scale.2: Child attempts validation but fails due to environment/build issues and does not find a workaround (e.g., direct module import bypassing __check_build)
scale.3: Child finds a way to test the fix (e.g., mocking dependencies, direct file execution, or successful build) but test output is not shown or is incomplete
scale.4: Child successfully runs a test showing the repr output matches expected format for both classes
scale.5: Child validates the fix AND tests edge cases (custom n_splits, n_repeats, random_state values) confirming all parameters display correctly

experiences.title: Distinguish script execution from bug reproduction: require exact error message in terminal output
experiences.description: When evaluating bug reproduction in exploration-phase rubrics, a reproduction script that runs to completion without the expected error is evidence of FAILED reproduction, not success. The judge must verify the exact expected error message and traceback appear in the terminal output. A 'Success!' result or normal output without the expected ValueError means the bug was not reproduced, possibly due to environment or library version differences.
experiences.context: In a FeatureUnion+pandas aggregation bug, the expected error is 'ValueError: Length mismatch: Expected axis has 4 elements, new values have 96 elements'. Some continuations ran the reproduction script but got 'Success!' with normal pandas output instead of the ValueError, likely because they used a different sklearn version where the bug does not manifest. These continuations did NOT reproduce the bug despite executing the script and producing output.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When evaluating exploration-phase rubrics that assess bug reproduction success, particularly where the rubric specifies an exact expected error message.

Positive evidence: The exact expected error message and full traceback appear in the terminal output (e.g., 'ValueError: Length mismatch: Expected axis has 4 elements, new values have 96 elements'). The continuation that shows this error has successfully reproduced the bug. Additionally, identification of the specific faulty function (e.g., _wrap_in_pandas_container or _wrap_data_with_container) in the assistant's text strengthens the reproduction evidence.

Contradictory evidence: The reproduction script runs and produces output but shows 'Success!' or normal output without the expected error. This indicates the bug was NOT reproduced, possibly due to environment or version differences. A script that runs without error when an error is expected is evidence of reproduction failure, not success. This is contradictory to any claim of reproduction.

Close-looking exclusion: Verify the script output contains the specific error traceback with the exact error message, not just that the script was executed. Check whether the environment matches the bug report (same library versions, same codebase path). A 'successful' run of a reproduction script for a known bug is actually evidence of reproduction failure. Distinguish between continuations that ran the script against the buggy codebase (testbed source) versus a pre-installed version that may already contain the fix. Also distinguish between continuations that only read code and identified the root cause (valuable but not reproduction) versus those that actually executed the failing scenario.

Reject misleading pattern: Do not treat 'script ran and produced output' as evidence of bug reproduction. The absence of the expected error in the output is contradictory evidence of reproduction failure. Running a reproduction script and getting normal output is no better than not running it at all for reproduction assessment. A continuation that reads code and correctly identifies the root cause location without running the script may deserve partial credit for root cause identification, but should not receive reproduction credit.

Abstention boundary: If the reproduction script has not been executed or its output is not visible in the paused state, reproduction success cannot be assessed and should not be inferred from code reading alone. If the script was executed but the output is truncated or incomplete, reproduction status is uncertain.

experiences.title: Do not use diff size or post-build investigation direction as a proxy for fix correctness when build output shows warnings persisting
experiences.description: When multiple trajectories modify the same validation file and all show the same warning count in build output, the fix is equally incomplete regardless of diff size or investigation direction. Score trajectories with equivalent visible outcomes equivalently.
experiences.context: A Sphinx toctree validation fix task where child trajectories modified sphinx/directives/other.py to recognize genindex, modindex, and search as valid toctree entries. Two trajectories both changed the same file and both produced build output showing 9 warnings persisting, but the judge scored them 0.4 points apart.
experiences.experience:
[Activation] When two or more trajectories modify the same source file and their build output shows the same number of persisting warnings.

[Positive evidence] Both trajectories show 'build succeeded, 9 warnings' in their sphinx-build output, confirming neither fix eliminated the toctree warnings for genindex, modindex, and search. This is the ground truth for fix completeness.

[Contradictory evidence] One trajectory has a 3-line diff (s01) and the other has a 13-line diff with 5 deletions (s03). One investigates toctree.py after the failed build (s01) while the other investigates docname_join (s03). These differences in diff size and investigation direction are misleading proxies for fix quality.

[Reject misleading pattern] The judge scored the 3-line change at 0.65 (highest, top node) and the 13-line change at 0.25 (lowest), a 0.4-point divergence. This divergence is unjustified because both trajectories share the same visible outcome: 9 warnings persisting. A smaller diff does not indicate a better fix when the build output proves the fix is incomplete. Post-build investigation of the warning source file does not compensate for a fix that does not work. The rubric's judge_focus explicitly requires 'build test showing warnings eliminated' — neither trajectory achieves this, so both should be scored at most 2 (weak progress, incomplete fix), not diverged to 3.6 vs 2.0.

[Close-looking exclusion] If one trajectory showed 0 warnings while another showed 9, the divergence would be justified — the trajectory with fewer warnings made more progress. The error only occurs when warning counts are identical but scores diverge based on non-outcome proxies such as diff size or investigation direction.

[Abstention boundary] If no build output is visible for either trajectory, cannot assess whether warnings persist and should not diverge scores based on diff size alone. If warning counts differ between trajectories, the trajectory with fewer warnings may deserve a higher score. If one trajectory shows warnings eliminated and the other does not, score them differently regardless of diff size.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Substantive Fix for Special Toctree Entries
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child trajectory adds a substantive code fix that allows 'genindex', 'modindex', and 'search' as valid toctree entries without generating 'nonexisting document' warnings, relative to the parent exploration baseline. The parent trajectories only explore the codebase (reading toctree.py, html builder, environment) without applying a fix. A child scores high only when it modifies the toctree validation logic (likely in sphinx/directives/other.py or sphinx/environment/adapters/toctree.py) to recognize these special generated pages as valid references, and ideally validates the fix eliminates the warnings. A child scores at equivalence (3) when it continues exploration without a fix. A child scores low when it loses useful parent analysis, makes invalid changes, or targets wrong files.

metadata.oracle_test: Build a Sphinx project with toctree containing 'genindex', 'modindex', 'search' and verify no 'nonexisting document' warnings appear
metadata.code_review: Check if changes are in sphinx/directives/other.py (toctree directive) or sphinx/environment/adapters/toctree.py (toctree validation) to add special page names to valid references
metadata.judge_focus: Visible diff showing recognition of 'genindex', 'modindex', 'search' as valid toctree entries; build test showing warnings eliminated
metadata.failure_mode: Exploration-only continuation without code fix; changes to unrelated files; fix that breaks existing toctree behavior; fix that doesn't cover all three special pages

scale.1: No meaningful progress: child only continues code exploration (grep, cat, sed) without any code change addressing the toctree validation, or makes changes to unrelated files that don't fix the warnings
scale.2: Weak progress: child makes a code change but it's incomplete (e.g., only handles one of the three special pages, or introduces a syntax error, or targets a file that doesn't control toctree validation)
scale.3: Equivalent to parent: child continues exploration/analysis without a substantive fix - same stage as parent baseline
scale.4: Strong progress: child implements a targeted fix in the toctree validation logic (directives/other.py or adapters/toctree.py) that recognizes all three special pages as valid, with evidence the fix compiles/runs
scale.5: Strongest progress: child implements a correct, complete fix for all three special pages in the appropriate validation location, and provides validation evidence (successful build test showing warnings eliminated)

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation of Warning Elimination
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child trajectory validates that their fix actually eliminates the 'toctree contains reference to nonexisting document' warnings for 'genindex', 'modindex', and 'search', relative to the parent baseline which has no validation. The parent trajectories only explore code without testing. A child scores high when it runs a Sphinx build with a test case containing these special toctree entries and confirms the specific warnings are gone. A child scores at equivalence (3) when it makes a code change but does not validate the warnings disappear, or only runs unrelated tests. A child scores low when it claims success without evidence or runs tests that don't exercise the toctree validation path.

metadata.oracle_test: Create a minimal Sphinx project with toctree containing genindex, modindex, search; run `sphinx-build -b html` and verify zero 'nonexisting document' warnings for these three names
metadata.code_review: Look for explicit test project creation, sphinx-build invocation, and output parsing showing the three specific warnings are absent
metadata.judge_focus: Visible evidence of targeted validation: test project with the problematic toctree, build command, and confirmation that 'genindex', 'modindex', 'search' warnings are eliminated
metadata.failure_mode: Running general test suite without targeted toctree test; claiming fix works without build evidence; build output showing warnings persist

scale.1: No validation: child makes code changes but runs no build test, or runs only unrelated tests (e.g., unit tests not exercising toctree)
scale.2: Weak validation: child runs a build but doesn't check for the specific three warnings, or test project doesn't include all three special toctree entries
scale.3: Equivalent to parent: child makes a code change but provides no validation evidence (same as parent's no-validation baseline), or validation is ambiguous (e.g., 9 warnings but unclear which)
scale.4: Strong validation: child creates a test case with all three special toctree entries, runs sphinx-build, and shows the specific 'nonexisting document' warnings for genindex/modindex/search are gone
scale.5: Strongest validation: child provides clear, targeted validation with a minimal reproducer, shows before/after warning comparison, and confirms all three special pages work correctly in generated HTML

experiences.title: Do not score exploration-to-implementation transition as a proxy for correctness when no edits exist
experiences.description: When all child trajectories remain in pure exploration with zero code changes, rubrics that reward identifying a likely fix location or narrating an exploration-to-implementation transition can create misleading process-level distinctions. Score concrete visible semantic evidence and preserve uncertainty about future patch correctness.
experiences.context: In a Sphinx toctree special-document warning fix task, all 8 child continuations at round 3 have made zero edits (current_patch_chars: 0, changed_files: None). The rubric 'Exploration-to-Implementation Transition for Toctree Special Documents' scores children on a 1-5 scale based on whether they identified the found_docs check in directives/other.py as the fix location.
experiences.experience:
Activation: every visible child has no code change and remains in exploration.

Positive evidence: mechanism-level reproduction, causal tracing, or explicit contract identification can receive diagnosis credit when it is actually visible.

Contradictory evidence: merely reading a likely source file, naming a line as the future fix location, or announcing readiness to implement is not evidence that the eventual patch will be correct.

Close-looking exclusions: do not collapse genuinely different diagnosis evidence into complete equivalence; distinguish concrete causal evidence from generic browsing, but keep the ceiling below applied and validated work.

Abstention boundary: do not predict final correctness or invent future actions when no implementation is visible.

experiences.title: Do not equate reading files containing rubric-named functions with identifying the divergent code path
experiences.description: When scoring exploration-phase continuations against root-cause localization and bug-reproduction rubrics, do not give equal credit to continuations that merely read files containing functions named in the rubric and continuations that locate the specific divergent function and its None-specific behavior. Do not score unfocused code browsing above empirical bug reproduction.
experiences.context: The issue concerns inconsistent cross-reference handling for None return annotations between signature mode (stringify_signature to stringify_annotation, producing plain text) and description mode (merge_typehints to make_xref, creating cross-reference nodes including for None). Two rubrics assess progress: root-cause localization (weight 1.2) and bug reproduction (weight 1.0).
experiences.experience:
Activation: When a continuation reads files that contain functions named in the rubric (e.g., stringify in typing.py, merge_typehints in typehints.py) but does not produce output showing it identified the divergence or the None-specific handling, verify whether the reading was targeted at the divergence or incidental browsing before assigning high scores.

Positive evidence: A continuation that greps for and finds make_xref's None-specific handling with 'obj' role in python.py demonstrates genuine root-cause localization. A continuation that runs the sphinx build, greps the HTML output, and confirms int gets a link while None does not demonstrates genuine bug reproduction. Both should score higher than a continuation that only reads code without these specific findings.

Contradictory evidence: A continuation that reads stringify in typing.py, annotation handling in inspect.py, and merge_typehints/modify_field_list in typehints.py—but does not identify the None-specific cross-reference logic or explain the divergence—should NOT receive the same score as a continuation that found make_xref's None handling. Reading files that contain relevant function names is not equivalent to understanding the divergence. A continuation that found the autodoc-process-signature event connection (a relevant part of the description-mode chain) should not receive the same low score as unfocused browsing of autodoc/__init__.py without any connection to the annotation processing divergence.

Close-looking exclusions: Finding the autodoc-process-signature event connection in typehints.py is relevant but does not by itself identify the divergence or None-specific behavior—it should score moderately, not maximally. Browsing autodoc/__init__.py for signature handling without connecting it to the stringify path is unfocused. Searching broadly for pending_xref or intersphinx without targeting the annotation processing divergence is not progress. Running the reproducer and confirming the int-link/None-no-link pattern is strong reproduction progress even if the description-mode comparison has not yet been verified.

Abstention boundary: If a continuation's visible prefix shows only file reading without output indicating whether the divergence was understood, and no reproducer was run, do not infer understanding from file-name proximity alone. Score should reflect the uncertainty of whether the reading was targeted or incidental. If a continuation ran the build but only in one mode, credit the partial reproduction but do not assume full confirmation of the behavioral difference.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Root Cause Localization: Signature vs Description Mode Cross-Reference Divergence
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The continuation demonstrates clear identification of the divergent code paths between signature-mode and description-mode return annotation handling, specifically locating where cross-references are created for type hints in each mode and explaining why None receives a cross-reference in description mode (via merge_typehints -> make_xref) but not in signature mode (via stringify_signature -> stringify_annotation which only produces plain text). Progress is scored relative to the parent baseline of general file exploration without pinpointing the exact divergence.

metadata.judge_focus: Whether the continuation identifies the exact functions and call chains where signature mode (stringify_signature in sphinx/util/inspect.py) and description mode (merge_typehints in sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py) handle return annotations differently, and explains the None-specific behavior in make_xref (sphinx/domains/python.py)
metadata.failure_mode: Stays at general file browsing without connecting the two modes' annotation processing paths

scale.1: No meaningful progress over parent: only general file browsing or reproduction setup without identifying the specific annotation processing divergence
scale.2: Weak progress: identifies one mode's annotation handling (e.g., finds merge_typehints or stringify_signature) but not the comparative divergence or the None-specific cross-reference logic
scale.3: Equivalent to parent: has explored similar files but hasn't connected why None gets a link in description mode but not signature mode
scale.4: Strong progress: identifies both merge_typehints (description) and stringify_signature/stringify_annotation (signature) as the divergent paths, and notes make_xref's special None handling with 'obj' role
scale.5: Strongest progress: clearly explains the full chain - description mode calls merge_typehints which creates pending_xref nodes via make_xref (which handles None), while signature mode calls stringify_signature which uses stringify_annotation that only returns plain text strings without cross-reference nodes

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Bug Reproduction and Behavioral Confirmation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The continuation has successfully executed the reproducer and confirmed the exact bug behavior: in signature mode (default), the return annotation 'int' gets a cross-reference link but 'None' does not; in description mode (autodoc_typehints='description'), both 'int' and 'None' get cross-reference links. Progress is scored relative to the parent baseline of code exploration without empirical verification.

metadata.judge_focus: Whether the continuation ran the sphinx build with the test configuration and verified the HTML output shows the specific link pattern difference between signature and description modes for None vs int return types
metadata.failure_mode: Only reads code or sets up files without executing the build and checking the actual rendered cross-references

scale.1: No meaningful progress over parent: only code exploration or file setup without running the reproducer
scale.2: Weak progress: attempted to run reproducer but encountered environment/setup issues (missing dependencies, wrong sphinx version, path problems) without reaching successful build
scale.3: Equivalent to parent: ran the build but did not check/verify the specific cross-reference output for None vs int in both modes
scale.4: Strong progress: successfully ran reproducer in signature mode and confirmed int gets link but None does not (grep output shows only int link)
scale.5: Strongest progress: successfully ran reproducer in both signature and description modes, confirmed the exact behavioral difference - signature mode lacks None link while description mode has it, with concrete grep/output evidence

experiences.title: Absence of oracle test run is not evidence of incomplete fix when sub-component tests pass
experiences.description: When a continuation shows visible positive test evidence at a sub-component level (e.g., unparse correctly handles tuple AST nodes with parentheses preserved), do not score it lower than a continuation with an equivalent diff but no test results. The absence of a full oracle test run does not prove the fix is incomplete, especially when sub-component tests demonstrate concrete progress. Conversely, a continuation that runs signature_from_str and shows defaults are still strings has visible negative evidence and should score below both positive-evidence and no-evidence continuations.
experiences.context: Fixing signature_from_str to parse default value literals as Python objects instead of strings. The fix involves the AST unparsing pipeline in sphinx/pycode/ast.py, specifically the visit_Tuple method. Multiple continuations modify this file with similar diff sizes, but their visible test evidence differs significantly: one shows unparse working for tuples, one shows signature_from_str still returning strings, and two show no test results at all.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When multiple continuations modify the same target file for the same bug fix and some show sub-component test results while others show none.

Positive evidence: A continuation that runs unparse on tuple AST nodes and shows correct output with parentheses preserved (e.g., '(1, 2, 3)' instead of '1, 2, 3') demonstrates the visit_Tuple fix works at the AST unparsing level. This is concrete visible evidence of progress that should rank above a continuation with an equivalent diff but no test results.

Contradictory evidence: A continuation that runs signature_from_str and shows defaults are still strings (e.g., default='(1, 1, 1)' with type <class 'str'> instead of default=(1, 1, 1) with type <class 'tuple'>) demonstrates the fix is incomplete. This visible negative evidence should result in a lower score than both positive evidence and no evidence.

Close-looking exclusion: Do not assume that because only unparse was tested and not signature_from_str, the signature_from_str path was not also fixed. A 2-line diff in ast.py may address both the unparsing and evaluation steps. The absence of a signature_from_str test run is not evidence that signature_from_str still returns strings. Do not conflate 'tested a sub-component and it works' with 'only fixed the sub-component.' Do not group a continuation with visible positive test evidence together with one that has visible negative test evidence.

Abstention boundary: If all continuations have equivalent diffs and none show any test results, do not differentiate scores based on which files were explored or what commands were run. Only visible test evidence (positive or negative) should differentiate scores among continuations with changes to the same file. If no continuation shows test evidence and all diffs are equivalent, score them the same.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Fix signature_from_str default value literal parsing
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the continuation fixes the root cause: signature_from_str must parse default value literals (tuples, ints, None) as actual Python objects instead of strings. The parent baseline (Parent 1 step 19) shows signature_from_str returns string defaults like '(1, 1, 1)' for tuples. Progress requires modifying the AST parsing/unparsing pipeline (sphinx/pycode/ast.py or sphinx/util/inspect.py) so that signature_from_str returns proper Python types (tuple, int, NoneType) for default values, and validating the fix against the reported rendering bug.

metadata.oracle_test: from sphinx.util.inspect import signature_from_str; sig = signature_from_str('(self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None)'); assert sig.parameters['color'].default == (1, 1, 1), f'got {sig.parameters["color"].default!r}'; assert sig.parameters['width'].default == 5; assert sig.parameters['label'].default is None
metadata.code_review: The fix must address how default values are parsed from the signature string AST. The visit_Tuple method in sphinx/pycode/ast.py must correctly unparse tuple literals, and signature_from_str must evaluate the parsed AST nodes as Python literals (using ast.literal_eval or equivalent) rather than storing the raw string.
metadata.judge_focus: Does the continuation produce a patch that makes signature_from_str return actual Python objects for default values? Does it validate against the concrete reproduction case?
metadata.failure_mode: Modifying unrelated files (domains/python.py, autodoc/__init__.py), only exploring without patch, fixing visit_Tuple but not the evaluation step in signature_from_str, or validating only via exploration commands (grep/cat) without running the oracle test.

scale.1: No meaningful progress: continuation explores unrelated files, only runs grep/cat/sed, or makes changes that don't affect signature_from_str's default value parsing.
scale.2: Weak progress: continuation identifies the correct file (ast.py or inspect.py) and makes a change, but the change doesn't fix the core issue (e.g., fixes visit_Tuple but signature_from_str still returns strings), or validation is only exploration output.
scale.3: Equivalent to parent: continuation has same knowledge as parent (knows signature_from_str returns strings, knows visit_Tuple is involved) but no validated fix applied yet.
scale.4: Strong progress: continuation applies a fix to the AST unparsing or signature_from_str evaluation that makes default values parse as Python literals, and shows evidence the oracle test passes or the rendering bug is fixed.
scale.5: Strongest progress: continuation provides a complete, validated fix where signature_from_str returns proper Python types for all default value kinds (tuple, int, None), the rendering output shows parentheses preserved, and no regression in real introspection path.

experiences.title: Do not score default-value-evaluation fixes by visible edge-case demonstration breadth
experiences.description: When judging fixes for docstring default argument rendering in Sphinx signature_from_ast/signature_from_str, do not use the breadth of visible edge-case test demonstrations as a proxy for implementation correctness. Solutions using eval(compile) and ast.literal_eval with fallback both correctly evaluate literal defaults (tuples, ints, None), but may demonstrate different edge cases in visible output. A solution that shows non-literal fallback (e.g., 1+2 -> '1 + 2') in visible output is not necessarily more correct than one that demonstrates only the core tuple-default fix.
experiences.context: The bug causes tuple defaults like color=(1, 1, 1) to render as color=1, 1, 1 because defaults are stored as unparsed strings. Two valid fix approaches exist: (1) eval(compile(ast.Expression(default), '<string>', 'eval')) evaluates arbitrary expressions, and (2) ast.literal_eval with try/except fallback to string for non-literals. Both correctly handle literal defaults. The judge gave a perfect 1.0 score to a solution demonstrating non-literal fallback in visible output, while scoring an eval(compile) solution at 0.769 despite both showing equivalent core fix correctness in visible evidence.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When comparing solutions that fix default value evaluation in signature_from_ast/signature_from_str, where one solution demonstrates more edge cases (empty tuples, single-element tuples, non-literal fallback) in visible test output than another.

Positive evidence: Both eval(compile) and literal_eval approaches correctly evaluate tuple defaults to actual Python objects. Visible output showing `color: default=(1, 1, 1), type=tuple` confirms the core fix works. Real introspection and bound-method paths producing correct `stringify_signature` output `(self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None)` are strong positive evidence of correct implementation.

Contradictory evidence: A solution demonstrating non-literal expression fallback (e.g., `1+2 -> '1 + 2'`) in visible output does NOT indicate superior implementation correctness. This visible demonstration reflects testing thoroughness, not implementation quality. An eval(compile) solution that evaluates 1+2 to 3 (integer) rather than falling back to string may still be correct for all tested cases. Explicitly reject the pattern: 'more visible edge-case tests = more correct implementation.' Visible test breadth is a property of the testing narrative, not the patch.

Close-looking exclusions: Solutions showing equivalent core fix evidence (tuple defaults evaluated correctly, same stringify_signature output `(self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None)`) should receive similar scores regardless of approach. A solution using eval(compile) that shows `color: default=(1, 1, 1), type=tuple` with real introspection and bound-method paths working has equivalent core correctness to one using literal_eval showing the same stringify_signature output. Do not differentiate scores based on additional edge-case demonstrations that go beyond the core fix. Solutions s00, s02, and s05 all show equivalent core fix evidence and were correctly scored similarly; the error was over-scoring s06 to 1.0 based on visible demonstration breadth alone.

Abstention boundary: When two solutions show equivalent visible evidence for the core fix (same stringify_signature output, same default types, real introspection working), do not attempt to differentiate their scores based on which approach (eval vs literal_eval) is 'safer' or 'more comprehensive.' If visible evidence cannot reveal a correctness difference for the core issue, score them equivalently. Do not infer implementation quality from approach philosophy or testing breadth.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Edge Case Handling and Fallback Robustness in Default Value Evaluation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child continuation correctly handles edge cases in default value evaluation for `signature_from_ast` and `signature_from_str` in `sphinx/util/inspect.py`. Parent 1 baseline: Continuations 1-4 use `eval(compile(...))` which handles arbitrary expressions but lacks explicit safety/fallback. Parent 2 baseline: Continuations 5-8 use `ast.literal_eval` with varying fallback strategies (Continuation 7 adds explicit try/except fallback). Progress means the child demonstrates correct handling of: empty tuples `()`, single-element tuples `(1,)`, nested tuples/lists/dicts/sets, non-literal expressions (e.g., `1+2`, `f()`) falling back to string representation without crashing, and consistency between `signature_from_ast` and `signature_from_str` code paths. Regression means breaking previously working cases, crashing on edge cases, or producing incorrect output (e.g., missing parentheses on empty/single-element tuples).

metadata.failure_mode: edge_cases_crash_or_render_incorrectly
metadata.judge_focus: Whether child handles empty tuples, single-element tuples, nested containers, non-literal expressions (fallback to string), and maintains consistency between the two signature parsing paths
metadata.privileged_reference_summary: Key edge cases: `()` -> `()`, `(1,)` -> `(1,)`, `(1, 2)` -> `(1, 2)`, `[1,2]` -> `[1,2]`, `{1:2}` -> `{1:2}`, `{1,2}` -> `{1,2}`, `1+2` -> `'1 + 2'` (string fallback), `f()` -> `'f()'` (string fallback). Both signature_from_ast (AST node input) and signature_from_str (string input) must produce equivalent results.

scale.1: Child breaks edge case handling: crashes on empty tuples, single-element tuples, or non-literal expressions; produces incorrect output (e.g., `()` renders as empty string, `(1,)` renders as `1`); or introduces inconsistency between signature_from_ast and signature_from_str paths. Clear regression vs parent.
scale.2: Child modifies default evaluation but handles only subset of edge cases (e.g., works for multi-element tuples but fails on empty/single-element tuples or non-literal expressions). Weak progress.
scale.3: Child matches parent baseline: for Parent 1, uses eval(compile) without explicit edge case validation; for Parent 2, uses literal_eval with whatever fallback parent has (Continuations 5-6 lack fallback, Continuation 7 has it). Equivalent behavior.
scale.4: Child implements robust edge case handling: correctly processes empty tuples `()`, single-element tuples `(1,)`, nested structures, and non-literal expressions (falling back to string representation via try/except or equivalent), with consistent behavior between signature_from_ast and signature_from_str. Clear progress.
scale.5: Child implements comprehensive edge case handling AND demonstrates it with explicit test evidence covering all edge cases (empty tuple, single-element tuple, nested containers, non-literal expressions, mixed annotations+defaults), with no regressions on existing cases. Strongest evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Default Value Evaluation in Signature From String/AST
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child continuation fixes the second half of the tuple default argument bug: ensuring `signature_from_str`/`signature_from_ast` in `sphinx/util/inspect.py` evaluate parsed default value strings to actual Python objects (tuples, ints, None, etc.) rather than storing them as strings. Parent 1 baseline: Continuations 1-3 implement evaluation via `eval(compile(...))`; Continuation 4 does not modify inspect.py. Parent 2 baseline: Continuations 5-8 implement evaluation via `ast.literal_eval` with varying fallback strategies (Continuations 5-6 lack explicit fallback, Continuation 7 adds try/except fallback, Continuation 8 uses helper function). Progress means the child modifies `signature_from_ast`/`signature_from_str` so `inspect.Parameter` receives real Python objects (tuple, int, float, None, bool, list, dict, set) for literal defaults. Regression means leaving defaults as strings, breaking real introspection path, or crashing on valid literals.

metadata.failure_mode: default_values_stored_as_unparsed_strings
metadata.judge_focus: Whether child changes signature_from_ast/str to evaluate default AST nodes to actual Python objects instead of storing ast_unparse output as string; handles all literal types; non-literals handled safely (eval or fallback to string)
metadata.privileged_reference_summary: Current code: defaults = [ast_unparse(d) for d in node.args.defaults] -> stores strings. Fix: evaluate each default AST node to its Python value. Real introspection (inspect.signature) already works; the string-parsing path used by autodoc for docstring signatures is broken. Two valid approaches observed: (1) eval(compile(ast.Expression(default), '<string>', 'eval')) - matches inspect.signature behavior for expressions; (2) ast.literal_eval with fallback to string - safer, matches literal-only expectation for docstrings.

scale.1: Child breaks default value handling further (e.g., makes real introspection fail, introduces eval errors on valid literals, or reverts to string defaults). Clear regression vs parent.
scale.2: Child modifies signature_from_ast/str but doesn't correctly evaluate defaults (e.g., still stores strings for some types, evaluates incorrectly, or crashes on valid literals like empty tuple). Weak progress.
scale.3: Child matches parent baseline: for Parent 1, Continuations 1-3 keep eval(compile) approach, Continuation 4 keeps string defaults; for Parent 2, keeps whatever literal_eval approach the parent has. Equivalent behavior.
scale.4: Child implements correct evaluation of default AST nodes so parameters get real Python objects for all literal types (tuple, list, dict, set, int, float, str, None, bool, bytes, ellipsis), with safe handling of non-literals. Clear progress.
scale.5: Child implements correct default evaluation AND demonstrates it fixes the end-to-end issue: `signature_from_str('(color=(1, 1, 1))')` produces Parameter with `default=(1, 1, 1)` (tuple), `stringify_signature` outputs `(color=(1, 1, 1))` without extra quotes, and real introspection path remains working. Strongest evidence.

experiences.title: Do not score equivalent patches differently based on verification test breadth
experiences.description: When multiple continuations produce patches with the same file modifications and the same correct observable behavior, rubrics must not differentiate them based on how many edge cases the agent tested or whether it demonstrated end-to-end HTML output. Test demonstration breadth is a process signal, not a correctness signal.
experiences.context: A Sphinx bug fix where tuple defaults like color=(1, 1, 1) were rendered as color=1, 1, 1. The fix requires two changes: (1) visit_Tuple in sphinx/pycode/ast.py to add parentheses, and (2) signature_from_ast in sphinx/util/inspect.py to evaluate literal AST nodes to Python objects with fallback for non-literals. Multiple continuations made both changes and produced identical correct output. However, the rubrics scored them differently because scale level 5 rewards 'demonstrates end-to-end correctness' and 'strongest evidence'—effectively rewarding agents that ran more verification tests rather than patches that are more correct.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When rubric scale levels include 'demonstrates end-to-end correctness' or 'strongest evidence' that reward test breadth rather than patch behavior, and multiple continuations share the same diff structure and correct output.

Positive evidence: A continuation that modifies both ast.py and inspect.py, evaluates literal defaults to Python objects (tuple (1, 1, 1) not string '(1, 1, 1)'), and falls back to string for non-literals (foo() becomes 'foo()') has achieved the fix. Any single correct test output like 'Signature: (self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None)' confirms the patch is correct.

Contradictory evidence: Running additional tests for nested tuples, empty tuples, frozensets, bytes, Ellipsis, or HTML autodoc output does not make an equivalent patch more correct. A continuation that tests only the bug-report case but produces the same correct output has an equally correct patch. The number of edge cases demonstrated is the agent's verification effort, not a property of the patch.

Close-looking exclusion: A real differentiator would be observably different behavior for the same input—e.g., one patch crashes on some_func() defaults while another falls back to string, or one renders (1,) correctly while another drops the trailing comma. But when both produce the same output for the same inputs (lambdas evaluate to function objects, calls fall back to strings, tuples render with parentheses, lists with brackets), the patches are equivalent and must receive the same score.

Abstention boundary: This experience does not apply when test demonstrations reveal actual behavioral differences between patches. If one continuation's tests show a crash, exception, or incorrect rendering that another's do not, the test is valid evidence of a real difference and justifies different scores. This experience also does not apply when a continuation only partially fixes the bug (e.g., modifies only ast.py without inspect.py, leaving defaults as strings)—that is a genuine correctness difference.

Rejection of misleading pattern: Rubrics that frame scale level 5 as 'demonstrates end-to-end correctness' conflate the patch's correctness with the agent's verification effort. The correct interpretation of 'end-to-end correctness' is whether the patch achieves correct behavior end-to-end (observable from any single correct test output), not whether the agent demonstrated it across many cases. Scoring agents higher for running more tests after an equivalent fix penalizes efficient continuations and rewards verbose ones without any correctness basis.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Literal Default Values Evaluated to Actual Python Objects
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child continuation modifies signature_from_ast in sphinx/util/inspect.py to evaluate literal default AST nodes (tuples, lists, dicts, sets, numbers, strings, None, True, False, Ellipsis) to actual Python objects instead of keeping them as string representations. Parent 1 baseline: Continuations 1-4 show the bug was identified but Continuation 1 only fixes visit_Tuple in ast.py (adding parentheses) while leaving defaults as strings like color='(1, 1, 1)'. Parent 2 baseline: Continuations 5-8 show the fix requires evaluating AST nodes to actual objects. Progress means the child changes signature_from_ast to use _evaluate_ast_node (or equivalent) on default values so that signature_from_str('(color=(1, 1, 1))') produces a Parameter with default=(1, 1, 1) (tuple) not '(1, 1, 1)' (str), and stringify_signature then renders it correctly with parentheses via object_description.

metadata.failure_mode: defaults_remain_strings
metadata.judge_focus: Whether child changes signature_from_ast to evaluate literal default AST nodes to actual Python objects (not strings), enabling correct rendering via object_description in stringify_signature
metadata.privileged_reference_summary: The bug fix requires TWO changes: (1) visit_Tuple in sphinx/pycode/ast.py to wrap tuples in parentheses, AND (2) signature_from_ast in sphinx/util/inspect.py to evaluate literal AST nodes to actual Python objects. Continuation 1 only does (1), leaving defaults as strings. Continuations 2-8 do both. The key semantic progress is (2) - without it, object_description receives a string '(1, 1, 1)' instead of tuple (1, 1, 1), and HTML rendering is still broken.

scale.2: Child modifies signature_from_ast but only handles some literal types (e.g., only tuples via visit_Tuple fix in ast.py) while other literals (lists, dicts, sets) remain strings. Weak progress.
scale.3: Child matches parent baseline: for Parent 1, only ast.py visit_Tuple fixed (strings); for Parent 2, has evaluation logic but may be incomplete. Equivalent behavior to parent.
scale.4: Child implements evaluation of literal AST nodes to actual Python objects in signature_from_ast (using _evaluate_ast_node or ast.literal_eval with fallback) for tuples, lists, dicts, sets, numbers, strings, None, bool, Ellipsis. stringify_signature renders them correctly via object_description. Clear progress.
scale.5: Child implements robust literal evaluation AND demonstrates end-to-end correctness: signature_from_str('(color=(1, 1, 1), items=[1,2], config={"a":1})') produces actual tuple/list/dict defaults, and HTML output via autodoc shows correct rendering with parentheses/braces. Strongest evidence.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Graceful Fallback for Non-Literal Default Values
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the child continuation correctly handles non-literal default values (function calls, variables, expressions like 1+2) in signature_from_ast by falling back to string representation instead of crashing. Parent 1 baseline: Continuation 1 only fixes visit_Tuple in ast.py with no inspect.py changes, so non-literals would crash or be mishandled. Continuations 2-4 add _evaluate_ast_node with try/except fallback. Parent 2 baseline: Continuations 5-8 all implement _evaluate_ast_node with robust fallback. Progress means the child implements a robust fallback (try literal evaluation, except fall back to ast_unparse) so that signature_from_str('(color=some_func())') produces a string default 'some_func()' rather than raising an exception, while still correctly evaluating literals like tuples to actual Python objects.

metadata.failure_mode: crash_on_non_literal_defaults
metadata.judge_focus: Whether child adds try/except around literal evaluation with fallback to ast_unparse for non-literal AST nodes (Name, Call, BinOp, etc.)
metadata.privileged_reference_summary: Non-literal defaults like some_func(), some_var, 1+2 cannot be evaluated via ast.literal_eval. The fix must catch exceptions and fall back to string representation via ast_unparse. Continuations 2-8 all implement _evaluate_ast_node with this pattern; Continuation 1 does not modify inspect.py at all.

scale.1: Child has no fallback for non-literals: bare ast.literal_eval without try/except, or no evaluation logic at all (e.g., Continuation 1 which only touches ast.py). Clear regression vs parent baseline that identified the need.
scale.2: Child modifies default evaluation but doesn't add proper fallback for non-literals (e.g., only handles tuples/lists/dicts via ast.py changes, crashes on function calls). Weak progress.
scale.3: Child matches parent baseline: for Parent 1 Continuations 2-4 or Parent 2 Continuations 5-8, has try/except fallback using _evaluate_ast_node or equivalent. Equivalent behavior.
scale.4: Child implements try/except fallback: tries ast.literal_eval (or _evaluate_ast_node) for literals, catches ValueError/SyntaxError/TypeError, falls back to ast_unparse string representation. Clear progress.

experiences.title: Do not reward diagnostic thoroughness when test output shows FAILURE with fragmented type tokens
experiences.description: When a continuation builds documentation and inspects HTML output that still shows the type rendered as fragmented per-character <em> elements, and the continuation's own test prints 'FAILURE: rendered incorrectly,' the rendering bug is NOT fixed. Score such continuations low on rendering-fix rubrics regardless of how many test files they create or how detailed their HTML inspection appears. Thorough investigation that reveals an unfixed bug is evidence of failure, not success.
experiences.context: A Sphinx doc rendering bug where :param dict(str, str) opc_meta: is rendered with the type split into individual tokens like dict(str, str). The parent baseline already fixed the type/name parsing (correctly yielding type 'dict(str, str)' and name 'opc_meta'), but the rendering path still splits the parsed type string into per-character elements. The rubric measures whether the continuation modifies the type rendering path to preserve the full type string as a single coherent node and validates the fix against the reported HTML output.
experiences.experience: Activation: When evaluating continuations against a type-rendering rubric that requires the type to appear as a single coherent annotation in HTML output, check whether the continuation's own test output includes rendered HTML for the complex type case. Positive evidence: A continuation that modifies the rendering path (e.g., TypedField.make_field or PyTypedField.make_xref) to emit the full parsed type as a single literal or inline node, and validates with HTML output showing 'dict(str, str)' as a coherent annotation rather than fragmented tokens, demonstrates progress toward the fix. Equivalent implementations that pass the full argtype string as a single Text or literal_strong node are valid. Contradictory evidence: A continuation whose test output explicitly prints 'FAILURE: rendered incorrectly' and displays HTML like 'dict(str, str)' has NOT fixed the rendering, even if it created multiple test files, built documentation successfully, and performed detailed HTML inspection. The fragmented tokens in the output directly contradict rubric levels 4-5. Do not reward diagnostic thoroughness when the diagnostic result is a demonstrated failure. The number of test files created and the detail of HTML inspection are process proxies, not correctness evidence. A continuation that locates the rendering code path (make_xref, make_field) but has not yet applied a change that produces correct HTML shows only code exploration, not a fix. Close-looking exclusions: A continuation that only runs existing pytest suites (e.g., test_ext_autodoc.py, test_build_html.py) without checking the specific dict(str, str) HTML output provides no evidence about the rendering fix either way. Existing tests passing does not confirm the new bug is fixed, nor does it confirm the fix is absent. A continuation that shows parsing test output (type='dict(str, str)', name='opc_meta') but no rendered HTML has confirmed parsing only, not rendering. Abstention boundary: If no continuation shows HTML output or explicit pass/fail for the dict(str, str) rendering case, and the correctness of the rendering path modification cannot be determined from the visible prefix, do not infer correctness from test-running activity, file creation count, or code exploration alone. Score based on visible rendering evidence only.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct complex type rendering in typed field output
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The continuation fixes the rendering of parsed complex type strings (e.g., 'dict(str, str)') in the generated HTML/output so they appear as a single coherent type annotation rather than being split into individual character/token elements. The parent baseline has correct type/name parsing but the type is still rendered as fragmented <em> elements. Progress is measured by whether the continuation modifies the type rendering path (TypedField.make_field, PyTypedField.make_xref, or related) to preserve the full type string as a single literal/inline node, and validates the fix against the reported HTML output.

metadata.judge_focus: type rendering in TypedField.make_field or PyTypedField.make_xref
metadata.critical_observable: HTML output shows type as single coherent annotation not fragmented <em> tokens
metadata.parent_baseline: parsing fixed via _parse_type_and_name but rendering still splits type into per-character nodes
metadata.preferred_evidence: ['modifies TypedField.make_field or PyTypedField.make_xref to pass full argtype as single literal', 'validates with test_autodoc_param3.py style HTML output check', 'shows before/after HTML for dict(str, str) case']
metadata.avoid_evidence: ['only tests parsing logic without checking rendered output', 'changes broad rendering behavior instead of type-specific path', 'relies on Napoleon parsing for raw :param fields']

scale.1: No evidence of addressing type rendering; continuation only tests parsing or explores unrelated areas, or the HTML output still shows fragmented type tokens like dict(str...
scale.2: Continuation identifies the rendering code path (e.g., TypedField.make_field, make_xref) but makes no change or only speculative changes without validating HTML output
scale.3: Continuation has behavior comparable to parent: parsing is fixed but type rendering remains fragmented; may have located relevant rendering code but not yet applied a fix that produces correct HTML
scale.4: Continuation modifies the type rendering logic to emit the full parsed type as a single node (e.g., using addnodes.literal_strong or a single Text node for the type) and demonstrates improved HTML output where the type appears as 'dict(str, str)' not fragmented tokens
scale.5: Continuation provides a localized fix to the type rendering path, validates with the exact reported case (:param dict(str, str) opc_meta:) showing correct HTML output 'opc_meta (dict(str, str)) – (optional)', and preserves simple type rendering (e.g., 'str name' still works)

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct native typed-field type/name split
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The continuation maintains the correct parsing of native Sphinx/reST typed parameter fields (`:param <type> <name>:`), where the parameter name is the final token and the preceding text (which may contain spaces, commas, brackets) is the full type. The parent baseline already implements `_parse_type_and_name` with rightmost-whitespace/parenthesis-aware logic that correctly yields type `dict(str, str)` and name `opc_meta` for input `dict(str, str) opc_meta`. This rubric verifies the continuation preserves this parsing behavior and does not regress to first-whitespace splitting or break simple/untyped cases.

metadata.critical_boundary: parameter name is the final token; preceding text is the type and may contain whitespace
metadata.preferred_evidence: ['locates generic docfield/Python-domain typed field handling in docfields.py', 'shows first-whitespace splitting truncates `dict(str, str)`', 'uses rightmost whitespace or equivalent logic to preserve full type', 'does not rely on Napoleon-only parsing for the raw field syntax']
metadata.avoid_evidence: ['patches only Google/NumPy docstring parsing', 'changes broad rendering behavior instead of the type/name split', 'keeps unrelated local environment compatibility workarounds']
metadata.judge_focus: type-name boundary parsing in docfields.py _parse_type_and_name
metadata.parent_baseline: parent already has _parse_type_and_name with parenthesis-aware rightmost split

scale.1: Continuation regresses parsing: reverts to first-whitespace split, breaks `dict(str, str) opc_meta` (produces type `dict(str,` name `str) opc_meta`), or breaks simple cases like `str name`
scale.2: Continuation shows parsing instability: modifies `_parse_type_and_name` in ways that risk incorrect splits for edge cases (nested brackets, callables, multiple commas) without validation
scale.3: Continuation preserves parent parsing behavior exactly: `_parse_type_and_name` unchanged and all test cases (complex types, simple types, no-type) pass
scale.4: Continuation preserves parsing and adds validation: runs targeted tests covering `dict(str, str)`, `Optional[Dict[str, int]]`, `Callable[[int, str], bool]`, and untyped params, all passing
scale.5: Continuation strengthens parsing with additional edge-case handling (e.g., trailing whitespace, multiple spaces, unicode) while preserving all existing behavior and adding regression tests

experiences.title: Reject pre-existing test failures and unrelated file reversion as regression proxies for docstring parsing fixes
experiences.description: When evaluating fixes to docstring parameter parsing in docfields.py, do not use pre-existing autodoc test failures (test_enum_class, test_autodoc_TypeVar) or typing.py compatibility fix reversion as discriminative evidence of regression. These signals appear in both correct and incorrect implementations and do not correlate with the semantic correctness of the parsing fix. Equivalent implementations that differ only in unrelated test output or side-file state must be scored equivalently.
experiences.context: A Sphinx docstring parsing fix for complex type annotations like dict(str, str) was being evaluated. The judge created rubrics penalizing continuations that showed failing autodoc tests or reverted a typing.py Python 3.10 compatibility fix. However, these signals are non-discriminative: the same test failures appear in both correct and incorrect implementations, and reverting typing.py does not affect the correctness of the docfields.py parsing fix. The judge inverted the branch ranking by treating non-discriminative signals as discriminative evidence.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When a judge rubric for a docstring parsing fix penalizes based on autodoc test failure output or typing.py reversion signals, and the same signals appear across continuations from different parent branches.

Positive evidence: HTML rendering output showing 'opc_meta (dict(str, str))' correctly formatted demonstrates the parsing fix works, regardless of unrelated test failures. A continuation that verifies rendering output produces the expected parameter format has positive evidence of fix correctness. A continuation that runs edge-case parser tests showing correct type/name splitting for dict(str, str), Optional[str], Callable[[int, str], bool] has positive evidence.

Contradictory evidence: The same autodoc test failures (test_enum_class, test_autodoc_TypeVar) appear in continuations from both parent branches, indicating these are pre-existing failures unrelated to the docfields.py change. A continuation showing these failures should not be penalized more than one that never ran the autodoc suite. typing.py reversion appears in both correct and incorrect continuations; the ImportError it causes is a side effect unrelated to parsing correctness. A continuation that reverts typing.py and shows ImportError can still have a correct docfields.py fix. Conversely, a continuation that preserves typing.py and shows no test failures can still have an incorrect docfields.py fix. Running unrelated test suites (e.g., test_util.py with 8 passed) does not constitute positive evidence of autodoc regression absence.

Close-looking exclusions: Attempting to run nonexistent test files (e.g., test_util_docfields.py) produces no test results and should not be scored as either positive or negative evidence. Running a broad test suite with deselected tests (e.g., 71 deselected, 0 run) provides no signal. The diff_stat and patch character count differences between branches (44 vs 43 lines, 3628 vs 2370 chars) suggest different implementations but truncated diffs prevent full semantic comparison — do not assume the larger patch is more correct. A continuation that submits early after showing correct rendering but before running regression tests should not be automatically penalized if the rendering evidence is strong.

Abstention boundary: When the full docfields.py implementation is not visible in the trajectory (diffs are truncated), do not infer correctness from proxy signals. The actual implementation differences require close code examination of the parsing logic. If the visible evidence only shows proxy signals (test failures, typing.py state) without the full implementation, score continuations equivalently and do not penalize based on non-discriminative signals. Do not reward continuations for running fewer tests or for avoiding test suites that reveal pre-existing failures.

experiences.title: Exploration-stage root cause identification does not predict autodoc typehint fix correctness
experiences.description: For Sphinx autodoc property type hint cross-reference issues, accurate identification of the code path divergence between PropertyDocumenter and method/function type hint processing should not be treated as evidence that a correct fix will follow. Diagnostic understanding and fix implementation are independent capabilities.
experiences.context: The issue concerns property type annotations lacking cross-references in autodoc output. The root cause involves PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header emitting :type: fields directly using stringify/restify, while methods/functions use the record_typehints/merge_typehints pipeline that adds cross-references. record_typehints only processes callable objects, skipping properties.
experiences.experience:
When evaluating exploration-phase trajectories for Sphinx autodoc type hint cross-reference bugs, do not treat accurate root cause identification as predictive of fix correctness.

Activation: Activate scrutiny when an agent articulates the root cause of property cross-reference failure during exploration—specifically when it names PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header, the direct :type: emission via stringify/restify, the merge_typehints/record_typehints bypass, and the callable-only filter in record_typehints.

Positive evidence: An agent may correctly identify that PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header emits :type: lines using stringify/restify directly, that this bypasses the merge_typehints/record_typehints pipeline used for methods/functions, and that record_typehints only processes callable objects (excluding properties). This demonstrates exploration depth and diagnostic understanding. Visible indicators include: locating PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header in sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py, recognizing the self.add_line('   :type: ' + objrepr, sourcename) call, reading sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py to find record_typehints, and connecting the callable-only filter to property exclusion.

Contradictory evidence: This diagnostic understanding does not predict fix correctness. The agent that most clearly maps the full code path divergence—naming PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header, the direct :type: emission, the merge_typehints bypass, and the callable-only filter—may still fail to produce a working patch. Conversely, agents performing simpler exploration (HTML output inspection showing attributes have reference internal cross-reference links but properties show plain text type names, stringify/restify behavior testing showing restify produces :class: cross-reference markup while stringify does not) without full root cause articulation may still arrive at working fixes through iterative experimentation or alternative approaches. The agent that states 'Now I understand the issue' after identifying record_typehints callable-only limitation and PropertyDocumenter direct :type: emission bypassing merge_typehints has demonstrated level 4-5 diagnostic understanding but has not demonstrated fix correctness.
