Prefer confirmed inherited source state when the parent persistent state explicitly records the applied fix; otherwise assign only moderate confidence to plausible but unvalidated implementations. Do not penalize an alternative implementation solely for not using the exact `output_classes` spelling, but do not award top credit unless the visible evidence shows correct per-output class handling and preservation of ordinary classifier behavior.

experiences.title: Do not top-rank unvalidated HTML-builder special-page diagnosis in the toctree generated-page warning task
experiences.description: For the Sphinx toctree task involving genindex, modindex, and search, do not give the sole highest rank to a continuation that has no edits and only observes that the HTML builder knows about generated pages. The decisive outcome is whether the toctree warning is reduced or eliminated, and unvalidated narrative about future tests or likely fix location is only diagnostic evidence.
experiences.context: In the paused judge view, several continuations investigate why a toctree containing genindex, modindex, and search reports nonexisting-document warnings. Some continuations modify sphinx/directives/other.py and then run a build that still ends with 'build succeeded, 9 warnings.' Another reproduces the issue with 'build succeeded, 3 warnings.' One continuation has no changed files, reads HTML builder code showing special handling such as search/genindex being recognized by the builder, inspects directives/other.py, and states that it understands the issue and will create a test. That no-edit, unvalidated diagnosis should not be ranked above branches with direct warning-count evidence or failure-driven debugging merely because it sounds confident.
experiences.experience:
[Activation]
Use this experience when judging paused continuations for the Sphinx toctree generated-page task where entries named genindex, modindex, and search trigger 'toctree contains reference to nonexisting document' warnings, and at least one continuation has no code changes while claiming to understand the issue after reading HTML builder special-page logic.

[Decisive positive evidence]
Highest credit requires visible outcome evidence: a build of a project containing genindex, modindex, and search in a toctree that shows the relevant warnings reduced or eliminated. Equivalent valid implementations are allowed: the fix may be in toctree resolution, validation, generated-page registration, builder support, domain/index handling, or another path, as long as it makes these generated pages valid toctree entries without regressing normal document checks.

When no clean or improved build is visible, give only limited diagnostic credit. Useful but non-decisive evidence includes reproducing the exact warnings, locating the warning emission path, discovering existing generated-page/special-target mechanisms, or testing a candidate patch and explicitly recognizing that it still leaves the warnings. A failed build result can be valuable for branch selection only insofar as the continuation uses it to invalidate a wrong approach; it is not evidence of a completed fix.

[Contradictory evidence]
A continuation with no changed files, no successful validation, and only a statement such as 'now I understand' or 'let me create a test' has not fixed the task. Reading HTML builder code that already treats search or genindex as generated pages is not enough: that code explains page generation or template linking, but it does not prove the toctree nonexisting-document warning has been suppressed. Likewise, a patch to sphinx/directives/other.py followed by 'build succeeded, 9 warnings' directly contradicts any claim that the warning-elimination fix is already correct.

[Reject misleading pattern]
Explicitly reject the judge bias or rubric pattern that promotes a confident no-edit diagnosis to the sole top rank because it found HTML-builder special-page predicates or identified a plausible future fix location. Confidence, file-reading, and intent to add tests are process signals, not correctness evidence. Do not rank such a continuation above continuations with concrete warning-count evidence or validated learning from a failed patch unless it also shows comparable applied progress or validation.

[Close-looking exclusions]
Do not require a specific file or exact patch shape. A correct solution need not be limited to directives/other.py, the HTML builder, or the toctree adapter if it preserves normal toctree behavior and validates the generated pages. Also do not treat every no-edit continuation as identical: one that reproduces the exact warning or traces the actual warning path has stronger diagnostic evidence than one that only browses unrelated files. Still, all no-edit diagnostic continuations remain below visible applied-and-validated warning reduction.

[Abstention boundary]
If no continuation shows a build after its changes, do not infer that warnings are eliminated from narrative alone. If every visible continuation is exploratory and unmodified, rank only by concrete causal evidence and keep the ceiling below implemented work. If builds are visible but all still show the same relevant warning count, do not create a large correctness gap based on diff size, confidence, or future plans; treat them as incomplete until warning reduction is shown.

experiences.title: No-edit toctree special-document round: do not rank line-spotting above concrete reproduction work
experiences.description: When judging the paused Sphinx toctree warning continuations with no source-code patch, prioritize visible, concrete reproduction/setup work and a correct warning locus over merely opening the warning line or asserting a causal theory.
experiences.context: The visible paused view is for the Sphinx request that toctree entries `genindex`, `modindex`, and `search` should not warn as nonexisting documents. Every continuation summary shows no source changes (`changed_files: None`, `current_patch_chars: 0`), so this round is diagnostic only. The visible evidence differs: some branches only inspect `sphinx/directives/other.py` or `all_docs`; some create or run a minimal Sphinx project; some produce `_build/html` artifacts; some make unsupported or incorrect causal claims.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when judging this paused no-patch round for the Sphinx toctree special-document warning task. Use only visible trajectory evidence: commands, outputs, summaries of untracked reproduction files/build artifacts, and assistant statements. Do not infer a final fix from future actions.

Decisive positive evidence for this round: Credit a continuation when it visibly moves toward a concrete reproduction or verification path, especially by creating both Sphinx project files such as `conf.py` and `index.rst`, running `python -m sphinx`/`sphinx-build` from that project, resolving missing dependencies in order to reach the actual warning, or leaving generated `_build/html` artifacts that indicate a build was attempted or completed. Also credit correct mechanism evidence when it is actually visible: the warning is emitted from the toctree directive’s `self.env.found_docs` validation, while `genindex`, `modindex`, and `search` are special/generated pages rather than ordinary source documents. Evidence such as finding the HTML builder’s `hasdoc` helper, `handle_page('genindex')`, index-generation code, or domain index metadata can support that mechanism when the continuation connects it to the `found_docs` warning.

Contradictory evidence: Do not rank a continuation highest merely because it displays the `directives/other.py` warning block or greps `all_docs`; that is line-spotting, not a demonstrated reproduction or full causal account. Do not treat a confident sentence like “now I understand” as decisive when the only concrete setup is a partial `conf.py` without a visible `index.rst`/toctree and without a build. Do not reward browsing `PythonModuleIndex`, standard-domain labels, environment storage, or generic toctree adapter code unless the branch ties those findings to the actual `found_docs` validation warning. A claim that the problem is the toctree adapter trying to access `env.tocs[ref]` is a wrong locus in this paused view; the visible warning source is the toctree directive’s missing-document check. A Sphinx run failing because of missing dependencies is not a reproduction of the three warnings, but dependency-resolution work is still concrete setup evidence and should not be treated as a semantic regression.

Reject misleading rubric/bias: Explicitly reject a judge bias that makes the branch showing only `sed` around the warning block plus `all_docs` greps the unique best branch. Also reject the opposite prose-only bias that ranks a branch highest for saying the pages are generated while creating only a partial test project. In this no-edit round, exact source-location discovery and fluent causal narration are weaker than a visible, runnable reproduction path plus a correct warning locus.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not require one exact future implementation. Equivalent valid fixes might add a special-document allowlist in the toctree validation path, expose a builder/environment predicate for generated pages, or otherwise make these names recognized at validation time. Do not collapse all exploration into equality: a complete reproduction scaffold or build artifacts are stronger than pure grep browsing, and a correct `found_docs`/special-page connection is stronger than unrelated file reading. But because no source patch or successful warning-elimination test is visible, keep all scores below implemented-and-validated work. Untracked build artifacts alone are positive setup evidence, not proof that the warning was reproduced, unless the warning output or the test source content is visible.

Abstention boundary: If a continuation has no patch and the visible evidence does not show either a concrete reproduction path or a correct connection between `found_docs` validation and generated/special pages, tie it with other partial explorations rather than making it a unique top. Do not predict final correctness from partial browsing, partial setup, dependency failures, or planned next steps.

experiences.title: Do not let synthetic signature_from_str edge-case breadth outrank the exact class-method AST/live-signature proof
experiences.description: In this paused Sphinx round, the strongest visible evidence is the branch that fixes both tuple unparsing and default-object construction, then demonstrates the reported class method through signature_from_ast with real tuple/int/None defaults and separately verifies the live and bound-method signature paths. A direct signature_from_str demo of the same text is valid positive evidence, but it is not automatically stronger, and broad synthetic edge-case output must not outrank the exact integrated class-method proof.
experiences.context: The user-reported bug is that a class method such as def add_lines(self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None) is rendered as color=1, 1, 1 instead of color=(1, 1, 1). The visible paused trajectories show two required integrated fixes: sphinx/pycode/ast.py must preserve tuple parentheses, and sphinx/util/inspect.py must construct inspect.Parameter defaults as real Python objects rather than strings. One branch visibly changed both files and printed signature_from_ast on a parsed BasePlotter.add_lines method as Signature: (self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None), with color type tuple, width type int, and label/name type NoneType; it also showed live-object and bound-method signatures still render correctly. Other branches emphasize direct signature_from_str or many synthetic edge cases, while some show defaults still as strings or only test a temporary helper.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when judging this paused round for the docstring/default-argument rendering bug, especially when a rubric or comparison prefers branches that call signature_from_str directly or print many synthetic default-value edge cases over a branch that proves the exact reported class method through signature_from_ast plus live/bound-method regression checks.

Decisive positive evidence: Treat as top-tier visible evidence a branch that (1) changes both sphinx/pycode/ast.py and sphinx/util/inspect.py, (2) fixes tuple unparsing so tuple defaults retain parentheses, (3) evaluates default AST nodes into real default objects, and (4) prints the exact reported method signature as Signature: (self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None) from signature_from_ast with runtime default types color=tuple, width=int, label/name=NoneType. The additional visible checks that live signature(...) on the class method still stringifies the same way, and that bound_method=True drops self while preserving color=(1, 1, 1), are strong regression evidence for the user-facing class-method path. Any implementation strategy that visibly achieves these behaviors without regression should be preserved as valid.

Contradictory evidence: Visible output where stringify_signature still quotes defaults, such as color='(1, 1, 1)', width='5', label='None', or simple defaults like a='0', b='0.0', c="'str'", is evidence that default values are still strings and the inspect.py half is incomplete. A branch that only changes ast.py, or only writes/tests a replacement function in a temporary file without applying it to the integrated inspect.py code, has not visibly completed the fix. A branch that demonstrates a literal-only fallback rendering an evaluable expression as a quoted string, e.g. color=1+2 becoming color='1 + 2', should not be treated as more robust than the exact class-method/default-object proof.

Close-looking exclusions: A direct signature_from_str output of (self, lines, color=(1, 1, 1), width=5, label=None, name=None) is valid positive evidence and can deserve high credit when backed by integrated code and no visible negative behavior. But it is not inherently stronger than the signature_from_ast proof on the reported parsed method, because signature_from_str parses text and then relies on the same AST-to-Signature construction. Extra demonstrations for lists, dicts, sets, annotations, empty tuples, or many literal types are useful but should not outrank the exact reported class-method proof with real default types and live/bound-method preservation. Do not require every parameter kind or every edge case unless the visible patch/output shows a real omission or failure.

Abstention boundary: If the paused view does not show integrated changes to sphinx/util/inspect.py or does not show either exact stringified output or default-object types for the reported signature, abstain from inferring full correctness from intent alone. If two integrated branches both visibly render the reported signature correctly with real defaults and both preserve the relevant live/bound behavior, score them equivalently rather than preferring a particular implementation style. If one branch has visible negative output showing quoted/string defaults and another has the exact real-object proof, the negative output is a real correctness difference.

Rejection of misleading rubric/bias: Explicitly reject the rubric bias that reserves the strongest score for direct signature_from_str demonstrations or for the broadest synthetic edge-case narrative. In this round, that bias undervalues the branch that proves the exact reported class method through signature_from_ast and verifies the live and bound-method paths. The judge should not rank verbose wrapper/edge-case demonstrations above the integrated class-method/default-object evidence that directly matches the user-visible bug.

experiences.title: Do not rank Sphinx property typehint continuations by confident diagnosis when no patch is visible
experiences.description: For the paused Sphinx autodoc property type-annotation cross-reference issue, exploration signals such as naming PropertyDocumenter, record_typehints, merge_typehints, stringify, or restify are not decisive evidence of a correct implementation. If the visible continuation has no code changes, do not score a confident root-cause explanation or a stringify/restify probe above other empirical reproduction work as though it proves fix correctness.
experiences.context: The visible task concerns property return annotations rendered as plain text instead of cross-referenced types in autodoc output. The paused continuations show only exploration: grepping generated HTML, inspecting PropertyDocumenter around property fget handling and :type: emission, reading typehint utilities, and testing that stringify returns plain module-qualified text while restify can produce :class: markup. The summaries show no changed files and no visible patch in these continuations.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply this when judging paused continuations for the Sphinx autodoc property type-annotation cross-reference bug where the visible trajectory consists of HTML greps, source inspection, or stringify/restify experiments, especially when the continuation has no changed files or visible patch.

Reject the misleading rubric/bias: Do not treat the deepest verbal root-cause localization, or the most confident statement such as “Now I understand the issue,” as the best branch by default. A rubric that rewards naming PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header, record_typehints, merge_typehints, callable-only filtering, stringify, or restify as though that predicts a correct final fix is misleading in this paused view. These are diagnostic observations, not implementation evidence.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer only visible evidence that an implementation has actually changed the relevant behavior. Strong evidence would include a patch that makes property type output generate parsed cross-reference markup, or otherwise routes property return annotations through an equivalent cross-reference-producing path, followed by validation showing the property type itself renders with a reference link. Equivalent valid implementations should be preserved: a property-local fix that emits appropriate cross-reference markup for the return annotation, or a broader typehint-pipeline fix that correctly handles property fget accessors and inserts the parsed type field, can both be valid if the visible behavior is correct.

Contradictory evidence: No modified files, no patch, and no post-change validation contradict any claim of implementation correctness. Merely observing that property output contains plain text like a module-qualified Point type, that attributes contain reference-internal links, that stringify returns plain text, or that restify returns :class: markup is reproduction/mechanism evidence only. A plan to extend record_typehints to properties is not decisive unless the visible code actually wires properties through that path and proves the property directive renders linked types.

Close-looking exclusions: Grepping raw HTML for any reference link is insufficient if the link belongs to an attribute rather than the property type. Stripping HTML tags can hide whether a type was linked, so plain-text grep output alone should not prove success. Source browsing around PropertyDocumenter or get_type_hints is not a fix. Testing restify on a dummy function return annotation is not equivalent to demonstrating fixed autodoc property rendering. Testing restify on the actual property fget annotation is useful mechanism evidence, but still not a patch.

Abstention boundary: If the visible continuation has no changed files or the relevant diff is absent, abstain from ranking branches by expected fix correctness. At most, score exploration subskills narrowly and keep similarly exploratory continuations close or tied. Only separate branches strongly when the visible trajectory includes an actual implementation and property-specific validation of cross-reference rendering.

experiences.title: Rank targeted FiniteSet–Interval complement semantics above compatibility churn
experiences.description: For this mixed FiniteSet minus Interval task, judge cumulative branch progress by the visible source semantics in the active complement path. A branch with only Python-version import fixes, existing-test passes, or broad unrelated edits is low-value unless it also contains a targeted implementation that classifies finite-set elements against the interval and preserves undecidable symbols.
experiences.context: The paused view shows the reported case `Complement(FiniteSet(x, y, 2), Interval(-10, 10))`. The visible dispatch probe shows `interval._complement(fs)` returning `Complement({x, y}, Interval(-10, 10))`, while `fs._complement(interval)` returns unrelated interval-piece expressions. The visible source around `Interval._complement` contains a `FiniteSet` branch that originally only collected numeric elements. Some continuations only repair `collections` import compatibility and run existing tests; those actions do not establish the requested FiniteSet/Interval complement behavior.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Use this when judging this paused round for the mixed symbolic+numeric FiniteSet minus Interval bug, especially when branches differ between targeted set-complement source changes and compatibility/test-running activity.

Decisive positive evidence: Prefer a cumulative branch whose visible source changes or source snippets implement element-wise handling for a FiniteSet in the active Interval/complement dispatch path, or in another location visibly proven to intercept the same `Complement(finite_set, interval)` evaluation. The implementation should ask whether each finite-set element is contained in the interval, remove elements definitely contained, keep elements definitely outside, and keep symbolic or undecidable elements rather than dropping them. Equivalent representations are acceptable if they preserve the unresolved symbols and known-outside elements without corrupting other set operations; do not require one exact spelling when the same semantics are achieved. A narrow change in the set-complement logic is stronger than broad environment or API edits.

Contradictory evidence / low-score conditions: A branch that only fixes Python compatibility errors such as `collections.Callable`, `collections.Mapping`, or `collections.MutableSet`, then passes existing tests, has not fixed this bug unless a targeted FiniteSet/Interval complement implementation is also visible. Passing `test_Complement`, `test_issue_9808`, or other existing tests is not decisive for the reported mixed case. Logic that only filters numeric elements and leaves symbolic/undecidable elements to be lost, ignored, or treated as definitely inside the interval is incomplete. Debug prints, new ad hoc scripts, or repeated reproductions do not compensate for missing source semantics. Broad unrelated churn should be treated as risk, not as evidence of correctness.

Misleading rubric or bias to reject: Explicitly reject the rubric bias that the fix must be in `FiniteSet._complement`; the visible paused view shows the reported expression following the interval-side complement behavior, and a `FiniteSet._complement`-only patch is insufficient unless it is visibly used by `Complement(finite_set, interval)`. Also reject the bias that import-compatibility work or existing-test success is comparable to a targeted semantic fix.

Close-looking exclusions: Source-selection or import-path investigation may explain why a run did not exercise local code, but it is not a substitute for the semantic implementation. A direct call to `fs._complement(interval)` producing interval fragments is diagnostic, not proof that the reported expression is fixed. A source snippet that merely still returns an unevaluated complement without showing element-wise classification should not be credited as a complete fix. Conversely, do not penalize a valid implementation solely because it is located outside `Interval._complement` if the visible evidence proves it handles the active expression with the same element-preserving semantics.

Abstention boundary: If the relevant complement source is truncated or absent and no verified behavior of the mixed FiniteSet/Interval case is visible, preserve uncertainty. If only compatibility fixes or unrelated tests are visible, score semantic progress as low rather than inferring an unseen fix. If both the active source semantics and a verified reproduction are visible, use them together, with source semantics decisive for distinguishing real fixes from test/environment noise.

experiences.title: Rank mpmath Rational fixes by emitted operand semantics, not by quoted whole-fraction wrapping
experiences.description: For the lambdify(modules='mpmath') Rational precision bug, a correct source fix must emit mpmath conversion on the numerator and denominator before division, such as `mpf(p)/mpf(q)`. A patch that emits `mpf('p/q')` or `mpf(p/q)` is a false fix and should score low even if it adds `_print_Rational` and inspect.getsource shows an `mpf(...)` wrapper.
experiences.context: The visible task shows lambdified mpmath source emitting `RisingFactorial(18, x) - 232/3`, causing Python to evaluate `232/3` before mpmath precision is applied. Several continuations edit or inspect `/testbed/sympy/printing/pycode.py` and `MpmathPrinter`. Visible bad outputs include `mpmath.mpf(1/3)`, `mpmath.mpf(-232/3)`, `mpf(-232/3)`, and `mpf('-232/3')`. One visible false-positive edit explicitly adds `_print_Rational` using `arg=repr(str(e))`, producing `mpf('-232/3')`; this must not be treated as a successful precision fix.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when evaluating continuations for the mpmath lambdify Rational wrapping issue where the paused view includes `MpmathPrinter`, `_print_Rational`, `sympy/printing/pycode.py`, `MpmathPrinter().doprint(S(1)/3)`, or `inspect.getsource(f)` output for a lambdified mpmath expression containing rationals.

Decisive positive evidence: The visible source edit or generated lambdify source shows that the Rational numerator and denominator are converted as separate mpmath operands before division. Examples include `mpmath.mpf(1)/mpmath.mpf(3)`, `mpf(-232)/mpf(3)`, `mpf('232')/mpf('3')`, `fdiv(mpf(p), mpf(q))`, or an equivalent implementation that ensures mpmath participates before the division is performed. A method like `_print_Rational` returning a format equivalent to `{func}({p})/{func}({q})` is strong positive evidence. The exact method body, quoting style for integer operands, or helper used need not match any single implementation as long as the emitted semantics separate numerator and denominator and avoid Python pre-evaluating `p/q`.

Contradictory evidence: Treat the following as incorrect, not merely incomplete: generated or printer output `mpmath.mpf(1/3)`, `mpmath.mpf(-232/3)`, `mpf(-232/3)`, or any method that passes the entire slash expression as the argument to `mpf`, because Python evaluates the division first. Also treat `mpf('1/3')`, `mpmath.mpf('-232/3')`, or a visible implementation using `repr(str(e))` for the whole Rational as a false fix: wrapping the whole fraction string does not create separate exact mpmath operands and should not receive high correctness credit. Raw output such as `1/3` or `232/3` indicates no mpmath Rational fix. Read-only grep/cat/sed inspections, environment setup, installing packages, or running tests without a source edit do not constitute a fix.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not give full credit simply because `_print_Rational` was added to `MpmathPrinter`; inspect what it emits. Do not reward comments claiming that string representation “maintains full precision” when the emitted string is the whole fraction `'p/q'`. Do not confuse `mpf('p/q')` with `mpf(p)/mpf(q)`: the former is the observed false-positive pattern, while the latter has the required separated-operand semantics. Conversely, preserve equivalent valid implementations: the fix may use `mpmath.mpf`, `mpf`, `fdiv`, quoted integer strings, or another printer path, provided the visible generated mpmath code prevents Python from evaluating the Rational before mpmath precision is involved.

Reject misleading bias: Explicitly reject any rubric or judging shortcut that awards top correctness for “adds `_print_Rational` using string format” or for `inspect.getsource` showing `mpf('-232/3')`. That source text is evidence of the diagnosed false-positive behavior, not proof of correctness. The branch with separated numerator/denominator mpmath conversion must rank above a branch whose only fix is whole-fraction string wrapping.

Abstention boundary: If the paused view shows only `changed_files` or `diff_stat` for `pycode.py` but not the `_print_Rational` body and not the generated source after the edit, credit applied-source progress but abstain from declaring semantic correctness. If the visible output explicitly contains `mpf('p/q')`, `mpf(p/q)`, or raw `p/q`, no abstention is needed: score that semantic fix low. If a continuation has only read-only exploration and no visible source modification, treat it as exploration only.

experiences.title: partitions(): prioritize a valid ms.copy code fix and file integrity over docstring keyword matches or edge-yield overreach
experiences.description: For the partitions() mutable-dictionary reuse task, the decisive visible evidence is whether the mutable ms dictionary is copied at the normal yield sites while the file remains syntactically intact. Do not rank a continuation highly merely because it inserts docstring phrases/examples if its sed edits visibly corrupt the docstring boundary or executable guard. Also do not require copying one-off fresh {} edge-case yields as if they were reused ms outputs.
experiences.context: Applies to the paused judge view for the task where partitions() in sympy.utilities.iterables reuses output dictionaries and the docstring contains a caveat about that behavior. The visible continuations edit sympy/utilities/iterables.py around the partitions() docstring and yield statements; some show tests proving distinct dictionary objects, some show standard diff submission changing yield ms to ms.copy(), and some show destructive docstring edits, syntax-error investigation, or doctest failures.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions:
- The user issue is specifically that partitions() reuses mutable output dictionaries and list(partitions(...)) can look wrong.
- The visible trajectory edits the partitions() function/docstring and shows evidence such as sed replacements, grep for yield.*ms, diff_stat, patch output, manual tests, doctests, or file snippets around the docstring closing triple quote and the n <= 0 guard.

Correct target:
- The mutable dictionary named ms is constructed, yielded, then mutated for later partitions. The normal output sites that return ms must instead return a copy of ms.
- Equivalent valid implementations include ms.copy(), dict(ms), constructing a fresh dict before yielding, or otherwise ensuring every yielded partition dictionary is a distinct object. For size=True, the tuple should contain the copied dictionary, e.g. yield sum(ms.values()), ms.copy().
- There are four textual normal ms-yield branches if size=True/False branches are counted before and inside the mutation loop: yield sum(ms.values()), ms and yield ms in both locations. These should be changed or made equivalent.
- The early invalid/zero-size edge case that yields a literal {} once is not the same mutable ms reuse problem. A fresh literal {} yielded once is not reused across multiple partitions and should not be treated as a required ms.copy() site.
- Updating the docstring to remove the stale caveat is useful, but a docstring phrase alone is not a substitute for a correct code fix and syntactically valid file. Do not require every possible doctest/example variant if the functional code fix is complete and the stale warning is not being relied on as the main fix.

Decisive positive evidence:
- A visible grep/diff/patch shows all normal yield statements returning ms have been changed to return a copy, including the size=True tuple forms and size=False dictionary forms.
- A final submitted standard diff begins with diff --git and includes the yield ms -> yield ms.copy() and yield sum(ms.values()), ms -> yield sum(ms.values()), ms.copy() changes.
- Manual tests after the final relevant edits show list(partitions(...)) has distinct dictionary objects, e.g. an id-based check prints True, and size=True results also contain distinct dictionaries.
- The file view after docstring edits shows a coherent docstring with a closing triple quote before executable code resumes, followed by a valid guard such as if (n <= 0 or ...). References/See Also sections are not accidentally swallowed into code or vice versa.
- A docstring update that removes “the _same_ dictionary object is returned each time” and replaces it with an accurate statement such as “A new dictionary is returned for each partition” is positive only when the surrounding file structure remains intact.

Decisive contradictory evidence:
- Any normal yield site still visibly returns the mutable ms object directly, such as yield ms or yield sum(ms.values()), ms, after the claimed fix.
- The continuation itself reports or investigates a syntax error, missing closing quote, or malformed docstring after its edits.
- A file snippet shows executable guard text such as “m and k and m*k < n):” orphaned without the leading if (, or code/comment lines appearing immediately after examples where the closing docstring boundary is not visible or has been deleted.
- A check for triple-quoted lines suggests the next function’s docstring appears before the current partitions() docstring is properly closed.
- Doctest output after the relevant edits reports failures in iterables.partitions, unless the continuation then visibly fixes the exact doctest/docstring issue and verifies again.
- The stale caveat “Note that the _same_ dictionary object is returned each time” remains as the authoritative docstring text after the final visible edit, especially if no submitted patch/code fix is present.

Close-looking exclusions:
- Do not give top credit to a continuation that merely inserts “Each partition is returned as a new dictionary object” plus plausible examples if the surrounding visible file is structurally corrupted by sed deletion or if no post-edit verification is shown after destructive edits.
- Do not penalize correct examples for dictionary key order differences such as {2: 2, 1: 2} versus {1: 2, 2: 2}; Python dictionary equality and the issue’s semantics do not depend on display order.
- Do not require .copy() on fresh literal {} edge-case yields. That is not evidence of the reported reuse bug, and a rubric centered on “all edge-case yields for n <= 0 must be copied” is misleading.
- Do not treat larger docstring diffs, more deleted lines, or more sed activity as better progress. In this view, large deletions around the docstring are often evidence of corruption, not completeness.
- Do not let docstring completeness outrank a complete, valid code patch that changes all normal ms-yield sites to copied dictionaries. Documentation is secondary to the functional mutable-reuse fix unless the stale docstring is the only remaining visible defect.

Abstention boundary:
- If the visible view does not show the final yield statements or a submitted diff containing them, do not infer the code fix from diff_stat alone.
- If a child edits the docstring after earlier passing tests, do not carry forward the earlier validation through later destructive sed edits unless the child visibly rechecks syntax/imports/doctests afterward.
- If the docstring closing boundary is truncated and no syntax/import/doctest result is visible after the edit, withhold full structural-validity credit rather than assuming the file is intact.

Explicit rejection of the misleading bias:
- Reject any rubric that ranks branches primarily by docstring phrase/example matching while ignoring visible syntax/docstring-boundary corruption.
- Reject any rubric that treats copying n <= 0 literal {} yields as required for this bug.
- Reject any judge bias that prefers a continuation with more documentation surgery over one with a complete visible ms.copy() implementation and a valid submitted diff.

experiences.title: Do not rank a paused non-submission above submitted Contains.as_set fixes based on extra manual validation breadth
experiences.description: For this Contains.as_set round, the decisive success signal is a final submitted git diff that changes Contains.as_set() to return the underlying set and updates the obsolete NotImplementedError test. Extra manual demonstrations over many set types are useful validation, but they must not outrank equivalent submitted patches, especially when the trajectory is still paused and has not emitted the final submission command.
experiences.context: Applies to the visible SymPy Contains.as_set task where the parent persistent state already identifies the intended fix: Contains.as_set() should return the set being tested for membership, so Piecewise can call as_set().as_relational(...) without AttributeError. In the paused judge view, the submitted continuations show the same essential diff in sympy/sets/contains.py, replacing raise NotImplementedError() with return self.args[1], and update sympy/sets/tests/test_contains.py to assert returned sets. One continuation performs broader manual checks for evaluated Contains and complex set types, but remains paused with no final COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT submission visible. The judge must not prefer that paused trajectory over continuations that actually submitted the equivalent valid patch.
experiences.experience:
Activation conditions: Use this experience when judging this round’s Contains.as_set continuations, especially when siblings have equivalent changed_files/diff_stat and the same essential implementation but differ in manual validation breadth or final submission state. It also applies when the parent state already records the simple intended fix, so children are continuations carrying forward and submitting that fix rather than needing a novel implementation.

Decisive positive evidence: Credit a trajectory highly when the final output is submitted and visibly begins with a standard git diff; the diff includes sympy/sets/contains.py changing as_set() from raising NotImplementedError to returning the underlying set, such as self.args[1] or an equivalent self.set; the diff updates the existing test_contains.py test that expected NotImplementedError into assertions that Contains(x, S).as_set() returns S; and visible checks show Contains(x, Reals).as_set() returns Reals and Piecewise((6, Contains(x, Reals)), (7, True)) no longer raises AttributeError. The final command `COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat ...patch...` with a `diff --git` patch is more decisive than additional exploratory tests.

Contradictory evidence: A trajectory that remains paused with empty/absent exit status and no visible final `COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT` submission should not be ranked above submitted equivalents merely because it ran more manual demonstrations. A trajectory that leaves as_set() raising NotImplementedError, returns the Contains boolean object itself, omits the Contains.as_set code change, or submits no applicable final patch has not completed the task. Visible Piecewise AttributeError after the patch would contradict correctness.

Close-looking exclusions: Do not treat broad manual checks of FiniteSet, Interval, Complement, ProductSet, or evaluated Contains as evidence of a better implementation when the underlying patch is the same simple `return self.args[1]`/`return self.set` fix. Those examples mainly demonstrate validation breadth; they do not justify putting a paused non-submission above submitted patches. Do not require special handling for evaluated Contains when the visible output only shows evaluated Contains becomes True and does not demonstrate a real regression in the submitted patch. Do not penalize a submitted correct fix because it lacks full set-suite or piecewise-suite execution if it already shows the direct issue fixed and submits the patch. Also, an unrelated failing test run performed after stashing the task changes is not decisive evidence that the submitted Contains.as_set patch is wrong.

Misleading rubric/bias to reject: Reject any rubric that primarily rewards comprehensive regression-test execution, complex set-type demonstration breadth, evaluated-Contains discussion, or semantic explanation over final patch submission and the essential code/test diff. Such a rubric will systematically over-rank a paused trajectory that merely tests more cases and under-rank submitted trajectories with the same valid fix. Testing breadth is secondary validation here, not a substitute for completing submission.

Abstention boundary: If the final submission status or submitted patch content is not visible, do not infer success from manual tests alone; mark the trajectory incomplete or abstain from preferring it over submitted equivalents. If two trajectories both submit applicable patches with the same effective Contains.as_set fix and compatible test updates, treat them as essentially equivalent even if one uses self.set and another uses self.args[1], or one demonstrates more extra cases than the other.
